title: Listening Lab
note: Latihan listening bertahap dengan suara sintetis browser: tangkap gagasan utama, perhatikan detail, lalu simpulkan maksud pembicara. CEFR adalah panduan editorial, bukan sertifikasi.

exercises.title: Missed the Bus
exercises.subtitle: Understand a short conversation about waiting for transport.
exercises.setting: Two classmates meet at the bus stop before school.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: I usually take the early bus to school.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Why are you waiting here? It is already seven forty.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: The first bus was full, so I am waiting for the next one.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: It arrives in ten minutes. We can wait together.

stages.label: Catch the main idea
stages.audioText: Mia: I usually take the early bus to school. Leo: Why are you waiting here? It is already seven forty. Mia: The first bus was full, so I am waiting for the next one. Leo: It arrives in ten minutes. We can wait together.
stages.prompt: What are Mia and Leo mainly talking about?
options: Waiting for the next bus
Choosing a new school
Buying a bus ticket for a trip
stages.explanation: Mia missed the first bus because it was full, and Leo tells her when the next one will arrive.

stages.label: Listen for a detail
stages.audioText: Leo: It arrives in ten minutes.
stages.prompt: How long will Mia wait for the next bus?
options: Five minutes
Ten minutes
Forty minutes
stages.explanation: Leo says the next bus arrives in ten minutes. Seven forty is the current time, not the waiting time.

stages.label: Understand the intention
stages.audioText: We can wait together.
stages.prompt: Why does Leo say, “We can wait together”?
options: He wants Mia to take a different bus.
He is offering to keep Mia company.
He needs Mia to drive the bus.
stages.explanation: Leo offers to stay with Mia while she waits. The sentence is a friendly offer, not a direction.

exercises.title: Booking a Study Room
exercises.subtitle: Follow a short exchange and identify a booking condition.
exercises.setting: A student asks a librarian about using a small study room.

focusWords.meaning: mempersiapkan diri atau sesuatu sebelum kegiatan terjadi

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Is the small study room available after three?

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: It is available from four, but you need to book it.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: We should prepare the slides before our group meets.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: You can use the room until six.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Great. I will make the booking now.

stages.label: Catch the main idea
stages.audioText: Maya: Is the small study room available after three? Librarian: It is available from four, but you need to book it. Maya: We should prepare the slides before our group meets. Librarian: You can use the room until six. Maya: Great. I will make the booking now.
stages.prompt: What does Maya want to do?
options: Book a study room for her group
Borrow a book for the weekend
Change the library's opening hours
stages.explanation: Maya asks about the room's availability and says she will make a booking.

stages.label: Listen for a detail
stages.audioText: Librarian: It is available from four, but you need to book it.
stages.prompt: From what time can Maya use the room?
options: Three o'clock
Four o'clock
Six o'clock
stages.explanation: The librarian says the room is available from four. Six is the time the booking ends.

stages.label: Understand the intention
stages.audioText: Maya: We should prepare the slides before our group meets.
stages.prompt: What can you infer about Maya's plan?
options: She wants the group meeting to be ready and productive.
She plans to cancel the group meeting.
She has already finished the presentation.
stages.explanation: Preparing the slides before the meeting suggests that Maya wants the group to use its meeting time effectively.

exercises.title: Changing an Appointment
exercises.subtitle: Understand a delay, a polite request, and a practical solution.
exercises.setting: Noah calls a clinic because his train is delayed on the day of an appointment.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Hello, Green Street Clinic. How can I help?

transcript.speaker: Noah
transcript.text: I have an appointment at two, but my train has been delayed.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: Would you like to reschedule, or can you arrive later?

transcript.speaker: Noah
transcript.text: Could I move it to tomorrow morning? I do not want to cancel at short notice.

transcript.speaker: Receptionist
transcript.text: We have an opening at nine thirty.

transcript.speaker: Noah
transcript.text: That works. Thank you for helping me.

stages.label: Catch the main idea
stages.audioText: Receptionist: Hello, Green Street Clinic. How can I help? Noah: I have an appointment at two, but my train has been delayed. Receptionist: Would you like to reschedule, or can you arrive later? Noah: Could I move it to tomorrow morning? I do not want to cancel at short notice. Receptionist: We have an opening at nine thirty. Noah: That works. Thank you for helping me.
stages.prompt: Why does Noah call the clinic?
options: He wants to ask for a different appointment time because of a travel delay.
He wants to apply for a job at the clinic.
He wants to complain about the clinic's location.
stages.explanation: Noah's train is delayed, so he calls to arrange a more suitable appointment time.

stages.label: Listen for a detail
stages.audioText: Receptionist: We have an opening at nine thirty.
stages.prompt: What time does the receptionist offer for the new appointment?
options: Two o'clock tomorrow afternoon
Nine thirty tomorrow morning
Three thirty this afternoon
stages.explanation: The receptionist offers an opening at nine thirty. Noah accepts it.

stages.label: Understand the intention
stages.audioText: Noah: Could I move it to tomorrow morning? I do not want to cancel at short notice.
stages.prompt: What does Noah's response suggest about him?
options: He wants to avoid informing the clinic.
He is trying to rearrange the appointment responsibly.
He no longer needs the appointment.
stages.explanation: Noah asks to reschedule rather than simply cancel, showing that he wants to keep the appointment and give notice.

exercises.title: Reviewing a Study-Space Proposal
exercises.subtitle: Compare evidence, recognise a concern, and infer what the speakers recommend.
exercises.setting: A student committee is reviewing a proposal to extend the campus study room's opening hours.

focusWords.meaning: cukup besar atau penting dalam jumlah, nilai, atau pengaruh
sedangkan; menghubungkan dua fakta yang berbeda atau berlawanan
melemahkan secara bertahap, sering kali kepercayaan, otoritas, atau argumen

transcript.speaker: Dina
transcript.text: The survey shows substantial demand for longer study-room hours during exam season.

transcript.speaker: Rafi
transcript.text: That is true, whereas evening attendance during ordinary weeks has barely changed.

transcript.speaker: Dina
transcript.text: Keeping the room open every night could undermine the budget if demand remains low.

transcript.speaker: Rafi
transcript.text: An alternative is to extend the hours only during exam periods and review the results after six weeks.

transcript.speaker: Dina
transcript.text: We should also consider the consequences for staff schedules before making a recommendation.

transcript.speaker: Rafi
transcript.text: Agreed. We need to compare attendance, operating costs, and staff availability.

stages.label: Catch the main argument
stages.audioText: Dina: The survey shows substantial demand for longer study-room hours during exam season. Rafi: That is true, whereas evening attendance during ordinary weeks has barely changed. Dina: Keeping the room open every night could undermine the budget if demand remains low. Rafi: An alternative is to extend the hours only during exam periods and review the results after six weeks. Dina: We should also consider the consequences for staff schedules before making a recommendation. Rafi: Agreed. We need to compare attendance, operating costs, and staff availability.
stages.prompt: What is the main purpose of this discussion?
options: To decide how to expand study-room hours while considering evidence and costs
To announce that the study room will close permanently
To compare different university examination systems
stages.explanation: The speakers weigh demand, budget limits, and staffing before recommending a change to opening hours.

stages.label: Listen for a contrast
stages.audioText: Rafi: That is true, whereas evening attendance during ordinary weeks has barely changed.
stages.prompt: What contrast does Rafi point out?
options: Demand rises during exam season, but ordinary-week evening attendance has barely changed.
The room is popular every evening throughout the year.
Staff availability increases whenever operating costs rise.
stages.explanation: Rafi contrasts substantial demand during exam season with almost unchanged evening attendance during ordinary weeks.

stages.label: Understand the recommendation
stages.audioText: Rafi: An alternative is to extend the hours only during exam periods and review the results after six weeks.
stages.prompt: What does Rafi's suggestion imply?
options: The committee should commit to permanent late opening immediately.
The committee should test a limited change and evaluate the evidence before deciding further.
The committee should ignore staff availability and operating costs.
stages.explanation: A limited trial with a review date allows the committee to evaluate real demand and costs before making a longer-term decision.

exercises.title: Finding a Lunchbox
exercises.subtitle: Follow a short conversation about a missing item.
exercises.setting: Two classmates look for a lunchbox before the next lesson.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: I think I left my lunchbox in the classroom.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: We can go back and look for it before the next lesson.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Thank you. I usually put it in my bag, but today I was in a hurry.

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: There it is, next to the window.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Great. We should arrive at class before the bell rings.

stages.label: Catch the main idea
stages.audioText: Mia: I think I left my lunchbox in the classroom. Leo: We can go back and look for it before the next lesson.
stages.prompt: What are Mia and Leo trying to do?
options: Find a missing lunchbox
Buy a new school bag
Prepare a class presentation
stages.explanation: Mia thinks she left her lunchbox in the classroom, so they go back to look for it.

stages.label: Listen for a detail
stages.audioText: Leo: There it is, next to the window.
stages.prompt: Where is the lunchbox?
options: Inside Mia's bag
Next to the window
Near the school gate
stages.explanation: Leo points out that the lunchbox is next to the window.

stages.label: Understand the reason
stages.audioText: Mia: Thank you. I usually put it in my bag, but today I was in a hurry.
stages.prompt: Why did Mia probably leave the lunchbox behind?
options: She was in a hurry.
She did not bring lunch.
The classroom was closed.
stages.explanation: Mia explains that she usually puts the lunchbox in her bag but was in a hurry today.

exercises.title: Checking a Booking
exercises.subtitle: Listen for a time, a condition, and a practical next step.
exercises.setting: A student checks a study-room reservation with a librarian.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: I booked the small room for our group this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: I noticed your booking. The room is available from three until five.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: Do we need to bring our own projector?

transcript.speaker: Librarian
transcript.text: The projector is already in the room, but please check the cable before you begin.

transcript.speaker: Maya
transcript.text: That helps. We can prepare the slides before everyone arrives.

stages.label: Catch the main idea
stages.audioText: Maya: I booked the small room for our group this afternoon. Librarian: I noticed your booking. The room is available from three until five.
stages.prompt: What is Maya checking?
options: A study-room reservation
A train ticket
A library membership fee
stages.explanation: Maya and the librarian discuss the time and conditions of a study-room booking.

stages.label: Listen for a condition
stages.audioText: Librarian: The projector is already in the room, but please check the cable before you begin.
stages.prompt: What should Maya check before starting?
options: The room number
The projector cable
The library opening hours
stages.explanation: The librarian specifically asks Maya to check the cable.

stages.label: Understand the next step
stages.audioText: Maya: That helps. We can prepare the slides before everyone arrives.
stages.prompt: What does Maya plan to do?
options: Prepare the presentation before the group arrives.
Cancel the booking.
Ask the librarian to prepare the slides.
stages.explanation: Maya says the group can prepare the slides before everyone arrives.

exercises.title: Improving a Study Routine
exercises.subtitle: Compare suggestions and identify the evidence behind a change.
exercises.setting: Two students discuss a study routine after reviewing their recent results.

transcript.speaker: Alya
transcript.text: Our practice results show that we remember more when we review in shorter sessions.

transcript.speaker: Bima
transcript.text: That is useful evidence, but we should check whether the pattern is reliable over several weeks.

transcript.speaker: Alya
transcript.text: I can maintain the routine if we review for twenty minutes after lunch.

transcript.speaker: Bima
transcript.text: That sounds manageable. We could also record which topics still cause problems.

transcript.speaker: Alya
transcript.text: Agreed. Then we can adjust the plan instead of repeating every topic.

stages.label: Catch the main idea
stages.audioText: Alya: Our practice results show that we remember more when we review in shorter sessions. Bima: That is useful evidence, but we should check whether the pattern is reliable over several weeks.
stages.prompt: What are Alya and Bima mainly discussing?
options: How to improve their study routine using practice results
How to choose a new university
Why they should stop reviewing topics
stages.explanation: They discuss short review sessions and whether their results support changing the routine.

stages.label: Listen for a detail
stages.audioText: Alya: I can maintain the routine if we review for twenty minutes after lunch.
stages.prompt: How long does Alya suggest reviewing?
options: Ten minutes
Twenty minutes
One hour
stages.explanation: Alya proposes twenty-minute sessions after lunch.

stages.label: Understand the implication
stages.audioText: Alya: Agreed. Then we can adjust the plan instead of repeating every topic.
stages.prompt: What does Alya imply about their next study plan?
options: It should respond to topics that remain difficult.
It should repeat every topic equally.
It should avoid using practice results.
stages.explanation: They intend to use evidence about difficult topics to adjust what they review.

exercises.title: Evaluating a New Schedule
exercises.subtitle: Separate headline figures from the wider evidence.
exercises.setting: A committee evaluates whether a university should extend evening study-room hours.

transcript.speaker: Dina
transcript.text: The latest survey suggests substantial demand for longer opening hours during examination week.

transcript.speaker: Rafi
transcript.text: Yes, whereas attendance on ordinary weekdays has remained almost unchanged.

transcript.speaker: Dina
transcript.text: A permanent extension could undermine the budget if the additional visits are limited to a few weeks.

transcript.speaker: Rafi
transcript.text: We might test the change during the next examination period and compare actual usage.

transcript.speaker: Dina
transcript.text: We should also examine staff availability and the cost of security.

transcript.speaker: Rafi
transcript.text: Agreed. A short trial would give us stronger evidence before a permanent decision.

stages.label: Catch the main argument
stages.audioText: Dina: The latest survey suggests substantial demand for longer opening hours during examination week. Rafi: Yes, whereas attendance on ordinary weekdays has remained almost unchanged.
stages.prompt: What is the committee evaluating?
options: Whether to extend study-room opening hours
Whether to remove the examination period
Whether to reduce the number of staff
stages.explanation: The speakers compare demand during examination week with ordinary weekday attendance.

stages.label: Listen for a contrast
stages.audioText: Rafi: Yes, whereas attendance on ordinary weekdays has remained almost unchanged.
stages.prompt: What contrast does Rafi identify?
options: Exam-week demand is higher, but ordinary weekday attendance has barely changed.
Attendance has fallen on every day.
Staff availability has increased substantially.
stages.explanation: Rafi contrasts substantial examination-week demand with almost unchanged attendance on ordinary weekdays.

stages.label: Infer the recommendation
stages.audioText: Rafi: Agreed. A short trial would give us stronger evidence before a permanent decision.
stages.prompt: What is the likely recommendation?
options: Run a limited trial and evaluate evidence before making a permanent change.
Extend opening hours permanently without further review.
Ignore staffing and security costs.
stages.explanation: A short trial would help the committee assess demand and practical costs before deciding.
